name: Gáe Assail
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: A spear and one of the four treasures of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
It returned to the thrower's hands after its bloody work.
Yelling ibar, the Gaelic word for yew, at launch meant certain death for the victim.
The inauguration stone stood at Tara.
His sword always found its victim.

text: The Gáe Assail is the spear of Lug Lamfhota and strikes like lightning. Its name, spear of Assal, remembers an earlier holder. Once thrown, the weapon flies back to the hand that cast it. If the thrower speaks ibar, the word for yew, the target cannot escape death. The sons of Tuirenn carried the spear to Lug as part of their debt. It counts among the four great treasures held by the Tuatha De Danann.

okr.objective: Describe the Gáe Assail as the self-returning spear among the four treasures of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
key_results: The Gáe Assail was one of the four treasures of the Tuatha Dé Danann
It returned to its thrower after its bloody work
Yelling ibar, the Gaelic word for yew, killed the victim
The other treasures were Dagda's cauldron, the Lia Fáil at Tara, and Nuada's sword
